operations.hypothesis: Replacing a pending 'buy now' with the best-matching unselected instruction-backed option value of the current page, and recovering tool calls written as reply text, makes the purchase satisfy the instruction's requested attributes; the guard leaves searches, product clicks and pages without instruction-backed options untouched, and switches off when H4 reports the turn budget is nearly exhausted.

The native tool descriptions say nothing about keyword choice or about option values gating a purchase; adding that policy to the two existing descriptions (content only, same names/schemas/order) makes the requirement contract visible on every call.

Publishing the page's unselected instruction-backed option values (and any click value that is not on the page) immediately before the solver call turns the failing pattern into an explicit next step, and the same snapshot lets H2 quote the pending requirement after a prose-only reply; guidance is only emitted when something actionable is pending and is deduplicated.

A cold-start procedure that keeps the observed tool-call discipline and search-keyword rules but adds the option-selection contract (select every instruction-named option value before 'buy now', match by meaning not spelling, go back instead of buying a product that cannot satisfy an attribute) gives the solver the goal -> progress -> next action contract from the first turn.

rounds.bundle_hypothesis: WebShop TRAIN failures concentrate on product pages whose clickable option values contain the values the instruction names (color/size/style/flavor/pack) while the solver clicks 'buy now' without selecting any of them (868, 820, 255, 806, 961, 425, 718, 932, 872, 893, 300), whereas every observed success either selected those values (874, 885, 947, 674, 341) or faced a page with no instruction-backed option at all (684, 720, 232, 1006). Deriving the instruction-backed option values from public history, tracking which were already clicked, warning before buying, and replacing only a premature buy-now (or an invalid/text-only action) with the single best-matching unselected value should recover several failures without touching any observed success.
